This page documents a proposed automated edit of the railway signals mapped in France, as required by the [[Automated Edits code of conduct]].

'''Status: proposal under discussion. No edit has been made.'''

== Who ==

* Operator: Noël Danjou ([[User:‹PERSONAL_OSM_ACCOUNT›]]), contributor to the [[OpenRailwayMap/Tagging in France]] page and author of the [https://noeldev.github.io/FrenchRailwaySignalling/ French Railway Signalling] JOSM presets and validator rules.
* Account used for the edit: {{User|RailwayMapBot}}. It is used for this edit only.
* Contact: ‹E-MAIL ADDRESS›, an OSM message to either account, or the forum thread listed under [[#Consultation|Consultation]].

== Motivation ==

About 17,600 railway signals are mapped in France. Their tagging was built over several years by a few mappers, with several spellings and key layouts for the same signal, and with typing mistakes. About half of the signals carry one of these variants. They are not rendered consistently by OpenRailwayMap and cannot be used reliably by other data consumers.

The corrections were first offered to mappers as a [https://maproulette.org/browse/challenges/57319 MapRoulette tag fix challenge], where each one is confirmed by hand. With close to 9,000 signals, this is long and repetitive work for the few mappers involved, while the correction is always the same for a given tagging. The automated edit applies these same corrections, and leaves to mappers the cases that need a human decision.

The corrections change how the data is written, not what it says: a signal keeps its type, its states and every other tag. This page does not claim that the wiki defines the only correct tagging. The corrections are limited to the list below, which is submitted to the discussion, and any of them can be withdrawn on objection.

== Scope ==

* '''Area''': metropolitan France.
* '''Objects''': existing nodes tagged <code>railway=signal</code> only. No object is created, moved or deleted. No geometry is changed.
* '''Tags''': keys under <code>railway:signal:</code> whose values belong to the French scheme (prefix <code>FR:</code>), and the few related tags named in the list of corrections.
* '''Volume''' (data of 20 October 2026): of 17,599 signals, about 8,600 would be corrected automatically, and about 400 are left to mappers.
* '''Frequency''': one-off edit, carried out region by region. It is not a recurring bot.

== Algorithm ==

=== Corrections ===

The corrections are those of the MapRoulette challenge and of the JOSM validator rules: all three are generated from the same public rule table, [https://github.com/noeldev/FrenchRailwaySignalling/blob/main/validator/rules.json validator/rules.json]. The complete list, generated from that table, is on [[Automated edits/RailwayMapBot/Corrections]]. There are four kinds:

{| class="wikitable"
! Kind !! Example
|-
| Renamed value. The value is matched as a whole item of a <code>;</code> separated list. || <code>railway:signal:main=FR:CARRE</code> becomes <code>railway:signal:main=FR:C</code>
|-
| Replaced tagging: keys renamed with their value kept, tags set or removed, when a stated combination of tags is found. A replacement is not applied when it would overwrite a tag it does not expect. || <code>railway:signal:speed_limit=FR:Z</code> becomes <code>railway:signal:speed_limit=FR:speed_indicator</code>, with its <code>:form</code> and <code>:ref</code> moved under <code>railway:signal:speed_limit:marker</code>
|-
| Redundant tag removed. || <code>railway:crocodile=yes</code> on a main signal, which implies it
|-
| Mistyped value of a key whose values are listed on [[OpenRailwayMap/Tagging in France]]: letter case, missing or doubled <code>FR:</code> prefix, wrong separator after the prefix, leading punctuation, a colon used as list separator, empty list items. The value is corrected only when this leads to exactly one documented value; otherwise it is left as it is. || <code>FR:cv</code> becomes <code>FR:Cv</code>; <code>FR:FR:S</code> becomes <code>FR:S</code>
|}

All the corrections of a signal are made together, so each node is edited once.

=== What is not changed ===

* Replacements that guess the intended tagging, or that need a complement only a mapper can give (a caption to complete, a board to map on its own node). They stay in the MapRoulette challenge and in the JOSM validator.
* Conflicting tags and undocumented keys or values: they are only reported by the validator.
* Free text (<code>ref</code>, <code>:caption</code>) and values of other schemes (Swiss signals <code>CH-FDV:</code>, <code>ETCS:</code>).
* A signal edited in the last 24 hours, so that a mapper at work is not disturbed.
* Signals of mappers who opted out (see [[#Opting out|Opting out]]).

=== Procedure ===

# The signals are listed region by region with Overpass.
# Just before each upload, every signal of the batch is read again from the OSM API, and its correction is computed on that current data. A signal corrected in the meantime is skipped.
# Each signal is uploaded with the version number that was read. If someone edited it in between, the API refuses the upload; the batch is then read and computed again. A concurrent edit is never overwritten.
# Changesets are grouped by region and hold at most 500 signals.

The bot only runs with the rule table that was discussed: it refuses to upload if the table has changed. Any change or extension of the corrections will be documented here and discussed before it is applied.

Dates: ‹TO BE SET AFTER THE DISCUSSION›. The series are recorded under [[#Log|Log]].

== Opting out ==

Any mapper can ask, by message or on the forum, that the signals they edited, or an area, be left untouched. The request is applied before the next series: the bot then skips every signal that mapper ever edited. An objection to a correction removes it from the edit while it is discussed.

== Reverting ==

Each series keeps the original tags of every signal it edits. A series can be reverted as a whole: the original tags are restored on every signal that nobody has edited since.
